hotspots.village: Chung Sam Wai, Fuk Hing Tsuen, Lam Uk Tsuen, Sai Tau Wai, Tung Tau Wai, Yeung Uk Tsuen (YL)
hotspots.use: texture (corrugated sheet, rust, whitewash, patching); roof form (low mono-pitch with timber edge); painted structure numbers as everyday detail; since 2026-10-17 (later) one of the four hut door kinds of the analogue view's illustrative switch: a flat sheet panel in a timber frame with a wire-mesh vent (reading the panel as a door is an interpretation; the painted marks are not drawn); since 2026-10-26 a layer of the analogue view's wall sets (tools/wall_textures.py); since 2026-10-26 the rust of the sheet roofs and drums (own_textures.py, rusty-corrugated-iron)
hotspots.why: A light-framed, sheet-clad hut on a footpath -- the kind of building the 1:1000 sheets draw dashed. On the same walk the author photographed a Lands Department notice "Do not build or purchase squatter huts" (IMG_8688, IMG_8689) and a gate signed 楊屋新村 155號 (IMG_8692): these huts are probably squatter structures in a non-indigenous settlement, the closest type in the library to the cleared KTN huts (an inference, not checked against a source).
hotspots.difference: Yuen Long, not KTN; patched for decades and of unknown date -- whether it stood in 1982 is not established; the painted numbers look like squatter-control marking but are undated; the air-conditioner parts are later.

hotspots.village: Chung Sam Wai, Fuk Hing Tsuen, Lam Uk Tsuen, Sai Tau Wai, Tung Tau Wai, Yeung Uk Tsuen (YL)
hotspots.use: texture (painted metal sheet, weathering); base detail (raised concrete plinth, pipes); vegetation growing over a hut; since 2026-10-26 a layer of the analogue view's wall sets (tools/wall_textures.py)
hotspots.why: Shows how a sheet-clad hut meets the ground and the planting around it -- detail the orthophoto cannot give.
hotspots.difference: Profiled steel sheet and the air-conditioner are later than 1982 and the paint may be recent; it stands on Long Ping Road, a busier edge than the pilot's lanes.

hotspots.use: wall texture (sheet over timber planks, patchwork); clutter (salvaged doors and windows, drum); since 2026-10-16 the wall texture TX06 of every temporary structure in the viewer (FN03)
hotspots.why: The author's own "saw" calls it a "squatter style building"; the patchwork of sheet and plank is the material language of the dashed temporary structures.
hotspots.difference: It stands in an indigenous village, its age and use are unknown, and the plastic tarpaulins are recent; the cleared KTN villages were mostly non-indigenous (CLAUDE.md section 9 rule 5).

hotspots.use: object model for the roadside shrine FP1458 (sheet 'Shr', 1980) if the author confirms it is the same place; elsewhere only where a sheet or the 1982 photo shows a shrine; modelled 2026-10-25 in the analogue view at its 1980 size (back wall and altar; textures TX10/TX11, matching_register.json AR24)
hotspots.why: Same village, 44 years later: same clan and building tradition, so the usual analogue caveats (CLAUDE.md 9.5) mostly fall away; what remains is rebuilding and re-surfacing since 1982. Shrines are rebuilt in place, so the form carries over even when the bricks do not.
hotspots.difference: Its date is unknown; the platform and kerb are recent. Never place a shrine without a source.
